text: W2's opaque-at-depth-d+1 tie is unreachable: an opaque boundary has no out-edges or direct facts, so the reachability prune drops it below depth 1.
evidence: W2 replaced by a reachable tie: seeds A (terminal, 2 hops) and Z (opaque, 1 hop, hand-built coverage unknown) on the first-hop callsite; A found first, Z sorts first; cap 1 must return Z.

text: 'Bounded by one frontier level' was false: post-cut nodes would still expand and push deeper terminals.
evidence: Design step 2: after the cut, nodes with depth >= cut_hops are not expanded and terminals with depth+1 > cut_hops are not pushed; only a same-length opaque hit remains possible.

text: The golden/no-change claim was too narrow: CDO hits the 256 cap (evidence, canonical keys, via_paths, conditionality, time can move), flags can move at exactly the cap, and a small --witness cap reaches this code.
evidence: Acceptance now: any golden movement triaged (truncated/path-limit at exact cap, path choice over cap), grep for non-default --witness, and a CDO digest byte-compare with every change explained plus a before/after timing.

text: The truncated gating was unspecified.
evidence: Revision 3: dropped_beyond_cut is set when a terminal is not pushed (depth+1 > cut_hops), when a node at depth >= cut_hops with an eligible expansion is not expanded, or when a post-cut node deeper than MAX_DEPTH is skipped; truncated = (cut_hops.is_some() && (!queue.is_empty() || dropped_beyond_cut)) || keyed.len() > cap; W4 (A, B->C, cap 1) pins truncated == true; a corpus oracle asserts the IMPLICATION (uncapped.paths.len() > 2 || uncapped.truncated) => capped.truncated (the flag is conservative, N3).

text: Post-cut pops count toward MAX_STATES and could introduce limit diagnostics; the prefix property cannot hold if a limit fires.
evidence: Since CR2 (T2) and F1 (T3): the loop guard peeks before pop, so no node beyond the cut is popped; pops after the cut are NOT counted toward MAX_STATES (digest.rs `if cut_hops.is_none() { state_count += 1 }`), so finishing the length class cannot newly trigger state-limit-exceeded. The post-cut work is bounded instead because no node pushes a child after the cut (F1), so it is at most the queue at the cut; W7 pins the bound. The prefix property is promised only when NEITHER the capped nor the uncapped run is incomplete; W8 pins a case where the uncapped run is incomplete and the prefix fails. Post-cut depth > MAX_DEPTH nodes are skipped without depth_exceeded and count as dropped.

text: check_witness_bfs already runs cap 2 and HARD_PATH_CAP over the r0 corpus.
evidence: check_witness_bfs (~:5340) runs cap 2 and HARD_PATH_CAP over the r0 corpus and, when BOTH runs are non-incomplete, asserts capped(2) == uncapped[..2] and (uncapped.paths.len() > 2 || uncapped.truncated) => capped.truncated. The corpus has no distinguishing witness, so it is a regression net, not a discrimination proof (W1-W8 carry the proofs).

text: merge_normalize_via_paths re-selects its top 3 by projected length/JSON, so the invariant is a raw-order prefix only.
evidence: Invariant explicitly limited to the raw reported order; the projection is noted as downstream and unchanged.

text: cut_hops recomputation was unspecified.
evidence: Recorded once with get_or_insert, never recomputed.

text: At exactly the cap, a dead queued branch made the old code report truncation; completing it clears truncation with no new path.
evidence: W3 pins truncated == false for the exact-cap dead-branch shape; the golden plan allows that flag movement.

text: An empty queue after the cut does not mean nothing was dropped: the new guards suppress paths without leaving queue entries, so truncated could read false on an incomplete capped witness.
evidence: Same fix as S4 (dropped_beyond_cut), pinned by W4 and the corpus truncation oracle.

text: W1 cannot discriminate the expansion guard (its leaves are terminals) and no state counter is exposed; W3 needs H's callsite to sort before D's.
evidence: The states-counting claim is dropped; the terminal-push guard is documented as a cost-only guard that no output can detect; W3 states the callsite order; W4 discriminates the truncation flag.

text: The exact corpus truncation oracle conflicts with the conservative dropped_beyond_cut: reverse reachability ignores visited ancestors, so an eligible expansion can dead-end (e.g. a cycle back to an ancestor) and the capped run reports truncated while the uncapped run has no further path.
evidence: Oracle changed to the implication (uncapped.paths.len() > 2 || uncapped.truncated) => capped.truncated; the conservative direction is documented in design step 3 and pinned by W5 (Root->A; A->H, A->D; D->E->F; F->A; cap 1 => truncated true, uncapped 1 path).

text: The loop guard must peek before pop/count, otherwise one node beyond the cut is counted toward MAX_STATES.
evidence: Design step 4: the guard peeks on queue.front() before pop_front and before the state_count increment.

text: Both post-cut guards (expansion and terminal push) are cost-only, not only the terminal one.
evidence: Acceptance: both guards are described as cost-only and gated only by the CDO timing.

text: 'Eligible expansion' was undefined.
evidence: Design step 3 (after CR1 and F1): a post-cut node at depth < cut_hops runs exactly the expansion filters (not visited, in valid_nodes, edge_has_hop) on its out-edges, by the same code the expansion uses, WITHOUT pushing; an eligible edge sets dropped_beyond_cut. A post-cut node at depth >= cut_hops takes an O(1) path: any out-edge sets dropped_beyond_cut (more conservative, allowed). W5 pins the conservative direction ('D's edge to E is eligible'), W3 the exact case.

text: S4's register evidence still quoted the old equality oracle.
evidence: S4's evidence now quotes the implication oracle.

text: path-limit-reached has two push sites, so which truncation cause fires changes its position relative to depth-exceeded and proof diagnostics; the 'cost-only' guards could change diagnostic order.
evidence: Design step 3: the post-loop site is gated on cut_hops.is_some() && (!queue.is_empty() || dropped_beyond_cut || found.len() > cap), so the diagnostic is pushed at the same site whatever the cause; the keyed.len() > cap fallback stays for the proof-only case.

text: After the cut the BFS still pops the whole cut-depth level, building visited chains and scanning out-edges only to set dropped_beyond_cut: up to a full BFS level of extra work per call on dense CDO roots.
evidence: A post-cut node at depth >= cut takes an O(1) path: no visited chain, no expansion scan; only a terminal-carrier check (dropped, sets dropped_beyond_cut) and an opaque check (kept at depth == cut); any out-edge sets dropped_beyond_cut (conservative). Commit 33a79418.

text: Post-cut pops count toward MAX_STATES, so a witness that used to be complete+truncated can newly come back incomplete with state-limit-exceeded.
evidence: Post-cut pops do not increment state_count; they are bounded by the queue built before the cut, so no witness newly reads incomplete from work beyond the cap.

text: A post-cut node at depth >= cut still builds visited_routines and filters all out-edges just to OR one bool.
evidence: Same change as CR1: the post-cut O(1) path skips the visited_routines build and the out-edge filter entirely.

text: After the cut, opaque seeds in the length class push opaque-or-unresolved-boundary diagnostics even when truncate(cap) drops their path.
evidence: After sort/dedup/truncate, opaque-or-unresolved-boundary diagnostics found after the cut (index >= diags_at_cut) are kept only when their routine ends a kept path, preserving order; pre-cut diagnostics never move. W6 (cap 1, seeds A terminal, Y and Z opaque) emits exactly the kept path's diagnostic; disabling the pruning fails W6.

text: The CHANGELOG claims exact-cap witnesses no longer read truncated because of a dead branch; that holds only when the cut comes from a terminal, not from opaque seeds.
evidence: The CHANGELOG now scopes the dead-branch claim to cuts made by a terminal; with an opaque-seed cut, queued deeper children still read truncated.

text: Stale performance prose cites pushed/popped counts measured when the BFS stopped at the cap.
evidence: The pushed/popped numbers are removed; the comment points to the arena note.

text: The post-loop path-limit condition has a redundant cut_hops.is_some() term, and two push sites are easy to desynchronise.
evidence: The redundant term is removed; the post-loop push site and the proof-only keyed.len() > cap fallback are each commented with why two sites exist.

text: Post-cut nodes below the cut depth are still expanded without counting toward MAX_STATES, so a wide fan-out (A->B at N callsites, B->C at N) materialises N^2 dominated nodes after the cut.
evidence: No post-cut node pushes children (BFS FIFO: every node queued at the cut is at least as deep as the cut level; a terminal child has hop_count >= depth+2, a non-seed opaque boundary is pruned by reachability). Below the cut depth a post-cut node only evaluates the shared eligibility filters to mark a dropped path; at or beyond it takes the O(1) path. W7 (A->B at 60 callsites, B->C at 60) asserts the arena stays bounded; re-allowing expansion fails W7 (arena 3663, bound 63). Commit after 33a79418.

text: The prefix guarantee was stated for the capped run only; it requires both compared runs to be non-incomplete (a 25k-sibling shape gives a complete cap-1 run and an incomplete cap-256 run with different first paths).
evidence: The ledger invariant and the corpus oracle require BOTH runs non-incomplete; W8 (MAX_STATES siblings, cap 1 complete returns Hb, cap 256 incomplete) pins the two-sided condition.

text: 'Nodes popped after the cut are not expanded' was false: nodes below the cut depth were still expanded.
evidence: CHANGELOG now says after the cut no node is expanded and post-cut pops are not counted toward the state limit.

text: The cost-only guards and the uncounted post-cut work were never timed on a workload that reaches the cap (the 3 CDO digests never hit it).
evidence: CDO release-fast: fingerprint --witness 1 over the whole workspace hits the cap 78,102 times; master 417.0/454.1 s vs branch 418.0/464.1 s (+1.3%, within the ~9% run-to-run spread); a 14-routine --witness all sample (150 cap hits) 21.5/19.1 vs 21.1/19.7 s. Output diffs are path choice only (2,191 cap-1 and 21 cap-256 witnesses); 114 sampled changed cap-1 witnesses each equal the uncapped first path.
